day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Calgary Airport at 14:00. Take the Banff Airporter shuttle (~$60 CAD one-way, book in advance for best rates) to Banff town (~1.5 hour ride). Check in to Banff Mountain Lodge and freshen up. Take a relaxed self-guided walk along the Bow River Trail through town to get oriented — free and scenic.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll Banff Avenue to explore the town. Head up to the free Tunnel Mountain viewpoint trailhead for a short 30-minute sunset walk with panoramic views of the Bow Valley. Grab a budget dinner nearby afterward.

meals.lunch: Grab a sandwich or snacks at the Calgary Airport before boarding the shuttle to save money on the road.
meals.dinner: Nourish Bistro on Bear Street — affordable plant-forward bowls and wraps, great value for Banff (~$15–20 CAD per person).

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a Parks Canada Discovery Pass on arrival (~$75 CAD per adult for the season) — it pays for itself quickly and covers all national park entry fees. Download the Parks Canada app for free trail maps. Confirm shuttle booking ahead of time.

day_by_day.morning: Early start for the Johnston Canyon Waterfall Hike. Drive or take the Banff Transit/Roam Bus Route 8X (~$6 CAD) to Johnston Canyon. Walk the suspended catwalks carved into canyon walls to reach the Lower Falls (1.1 km) and Upper Falls (2.7 km return). Arrive before 9:00 AM to beat crowds. The trail is well-marked and mostly flat — great for all fitness levels.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue past the Upper Falls to the Ink Pots — seven cold mineral springs in a beautiful open meadow (~11 km return total from trailhead). Pack a lunch to eat at the Ink Pots and enjoy the solitude. Return to Banff by early afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Rest at the lodge, then take a free evening walk around Vermilion Lakes — a 5 km flat loop with stunning mountain reflections and excellent wildlife spotting (elk, beaver, herons). One of Banff's best free experiences.

meals.breakfast: Self-cater at the lodge — pick up oats, fruit, and yogurt from Nesters Market (Banff's local grocery store) the night before to save significantly on morning meals.
meals.lunch: Pack a homemade lunch from the lodge — sandwiches, trail mix, and fruit. Eat at the Ink Pots meadow.
meals.dinner: Banff Ave Brewing Co. — try their affordable pub-style burgers and nachos with a local craft beer. Happy hour deals available (~$18–25 CAD per person).

day_by_day.notes: Roam Bus Route 8X runs seasonally to Johnston Canyon — check current schedule at roamtransit.com. Wear layers; the canyon can be cool and moist even in summer. The Ink Pots extension adds ~3 hours but is highly recommended and completely free.

day_by_day.morning: Big day — Moraine Lake Valley of the Ten Peaks Trek. Due to high demand, private vehicles are not permitted at Moraine Lake in peak season. Book the Parks Canada Moraine Lake shuttle in advance (~$8 CAD each way from Banff). Depart by 6:30 AM to catch an early shuttle. Hike the Rockpile Trail first (20-minute loop) for the iconic panoramic view of the turquoise lake and Valley of the Ten Peaks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue onto the Lakeshore Trail (3.4 km return, flat and easy) hugging the shoreline of Moraine Lake. Enjoy the vivid blue-green glacial water up close. Bring your own lunch and eat at the lakeshore. Explore the area fully before catching the return shuttle to Banff in the early afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening in town. Walk up to the Banff Centre Hill for free views, or browse the free Whyte Museum of the Canadian Rockies (free on Thursday evenings, otherwise ~$10 CAD) to learn about the region's history and Indigenous culture.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered early breakfast at the lodge — overnight oats or granola bars to eat on the go before the shuttle.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from Nesters Market — wraps, cheese, crackers, and fruit eaten at the Moraine Lake shoreline.
meals.dinner: Melissa's Missteak on Lynx Street — a Banff institution with generous portions. Order the soup and sandwich combo or pasta for a filling budget-friendly meal (~$18–22 CAD).

day_by_day.notes: Moraine Lake shuttle tickets MUST be booked in advance on the Parks Canada reservation system — they sell out weeks ahead. Bring a jacket; the lake sits at 1,885 m elevation and mornings can be cool. No food or drinks to be left unattended — bear country protocols apply.

day_by_day.morning: Icefields Parkway Scenic Drive — one of the world's most spectacular highways. Rent a car for the day (~$60–80 CAD, shared cost if traveling with others) or join a budget group day tour (~$80–100 CAD). Head north on Highway 93. First stop: Bow Lake (~55 km from Banff) — short flat lakeshore walk with stunning turquoise water and Crowfoot Glacier views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Bow Summit (the highest drivable point on the Parkway at 2,069 m) for the Peyto Lake Viewpoint hike — a 1.6 km return walk to one of the most breathtaking lake views in the Rockies. The wolf-head shaped electric-blue lake is unmissable. Drive back south with stops at Mistaya Canyon (short 400 m walk to a dramatic limestone gorge) and the Weeping Wall if time permits.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Banff by early evening. Treat yourself to a soak at the Banff Upper Hot Springs (~$20 CAD entry) — a well-earned reward after a big day of driving and hiking with gorgeous mountain views.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at the lodge — fuel up before the long drive.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Peyto Lake viewpoint or Bow Lake. There are no affordable food options along the Parkway — packing food is essential and saves $20–30 CAD.
meals.dinner: Nesters Market deli section or Safeway — pick up a rotisserie chicken, salad, and bread for a self-catered dinner back at the lodge to offset the car rental cost.

day_by_day.notes: A Parks Canada pass is required for the Icefields Parkway — already covered if you purchased the Discovery Pass on Day 1. Fill up the gas tank in Banff before departing; fuel on the Parkway is very expensive. Start the drive early to avoid afternoon tour bus crowds at Peyto Lake.

day_by_day.morning: Sulphur Mountain hike — skip the gondola ($60+ CAD) and hike up for free! The Sulphur Mountain Trail is 5.5 km one-way with 655 m elevation gain, taking about 2 hours up. The trail is well-maintained and the summit views over Banff townsite, the Bow Valley, and surrounding peaks are spectacular. Ride the gondola down for free (one-way descent is complimentary with proof of hiking up).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Banff Cosmic Ray Station at the summit (a National Historic Site, free to enter) and walk the Sanson Peak boardwalk. Descend and head to Lake Minnewanka — take the free Roam Bus or drive. Walk the easy Lake Minnewanka Lakeshore Trail (as far as you like — the full trail is 28 km but even 3–5 km out-and-back is rewarding with stunning mountain-framed lake views).
day_by_day.evening: Head to Two Jack Lake (adjacent to Lake Minnewanka, free access with Parks pass) for golden hour photography and a peaceful lakeside stroll. Return to town for a final budget dinner.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at the lodge — a hearty breakfast before the Sulphur Mountain climb.
meals.lunch: Pack lunch to eat at the Sulphur Mountain summit — enjoy the views without paying gondola restaurant prices.
meals.dinner: The Elk & Oarsman on Banff Avenue — try their daily specials and affordable pasta or burger options (~$18–24 CAD). Lively atmosphere great for a social budget dinner.

day_by_day.notes: Start the Sulphur Mountain hike early (before 8 AM) to avoid heat and crowds. Bring trekking poles if available — the descent can be hard on knees. Confirm the free gondola descent policy hasn't changed by checking the Banff Gondola website before your trip.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — sunrise walk at Cascade Ponds or a peaceful stroll along the Bow River Pathway through town (free, flat, beautiful). Visit the Banff Farmers Market if it falls on a weekend for local snacks and souvenirs at reasonable prices. Last-minute souvenir shopping on Banff Avenue — look for affordable keepsakes at Banff Trading Post or the Parks Canada gift shop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time, squeeze in a visit to Johnson Lake (free, 10 minutes from town) for a final swim in a warmer-than-usual Rockies lake surrounded by forest — a hidden gem compared to the busier lakes. Pack up, check out of Banff Mountain Lodge, and catch the Banff Airporter shuttle back to Calgary Airport.
day_by_day.evening: Travel day — flight departure from Calgary. Grab a final meal at the Calgary Airport or bring snacks from Banff.

meals.breakfast: Final self-catered breakfast at the lodge using any remaining groceries from Nesters Market — clear out your food supplies before checkout.
meals.lunch: Wild Flour Artisan Bakery on Bear Street — excellent fresh-baked sandwiches, pastries, and coffee at very reasonable Banff prices (~$12–15 CAD). A perfect final Banff meal.
meals.dinner: Airport meal or packed snacks for the flight home.

day_by_day.notes: Book the return Banff Airporter shuttle in advance and confirm the pickup time from your hotel. Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for the shuttle ride plus airport security. Johnson Lake is a great final stop only if your departure shuttle allows time — it's close to the Lake Minnewanka loop road. Leave no trace — pack out all waste from trails and campsites.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 14:00. Travel from Calgary International Airport to Banff Mountain Lodge (~1.5 hour drive via Trans-Canada Highway). Settle into your room and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore downtown Banff on foot. Stroll along Banff Avenue, visit the Banff Visitor Centre to pick up park passes and trail maps, and take a short walk to the Bow River Falls viewpoint – a gentle 10-minute walk from downtown. Great way to ease into the mountain scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset stroll along the Bow River Trail near the hotel, then relax and prepare for the week ahead. Browse the shops along Banff Avenue if energy allows.

meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at the Calgary airport before departure or pack snacks for the drive.
meals.dinner: Dinner at The Bison Restaurant & Terrace on Bear Street – locally sourced Canadian cuisine with mountain views, mains ~CAD $28–$42. Great introduction to Banff dining.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase your Parks Canada Discovery Pass upon arrival if you don't have one (~CAD $75.25/adult for an annual pass – worth it for a 6-day trip). Book Moraine Lake shuttle tickets online tonight if not already done, as access is restricted and shuttles sell out weeks in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Early start – Moraine Lake Valley of the Ten Peaks Trek. Take the Parks Canada shuttle from the Banff Gondola staging area (departs ~8:00 AM). Hike the Rockpile Trail first for the iconic panoramic photo, then continue along the Lakeshore Trail (5.6 km round trip, easy-moderate). The turquoise water and Valley of the Ten Peaks backdrop is absolutely breathtaking in morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return via shuttle to Banff by early afternoon. Stop at Lake Louise Village on the way back for a coffee break, then check out the Lake Louise Lakeshore for a relaxed walk along the shoreline (30–45 min stroll) to preview tomorrow's full hike experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Banff. Relax at the hotel. Optional: visit the Banff Upper Hot Springs (~CAD $16/adult) to soak tired muscles after the day's hiking.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel or grab a packed breakfast/coffee from Whitebark Café on Bear Street before the shuttle.
meals.lunch: Pack a trail lunch – sandwiches and snacks from Nesters Market grocery store (stock up the night before). Eat at Moraine Lake with the view.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Tooloulou's on Banff Avenue – Cajun-inspired comfort food, lively atmosphere, mains ~CAD $20–$32. Great mid-range option.

day_by_day.notes: Moraine Lake shuttle tickets must be pre-booked through the Parks Canada reservation system. Wear layers – mornings at Moraine Lake can be cool even in July (~10–14°C at dawn). Bring sunscreen and plenty of water. The Lakeshore Trail is mostly flat and suitable for all fitness levels.

day_by_day.morning: Lake Louise Hike & Canoe experience. Take the shuttle or drive to Lake Louise (45 min from Banff). Begin with the Plain of Six Glaciers Trail (13.8 km round trip, moderate) – hike past the iconic lake shoreline, through alpine meadows, and up to the historic Plain of Six Glaciers Teahouse with views of Victoria Glacier. Start by 8:00–8:30 AM for the best light and to beat crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: After returning from the hike, rent a canoe at the Lake Louise Boathouse (CAD ~$155/hour for a canoe, fits 2–3 people) for a 1-hour paddle on the stunning jade-green waters with the Fairmont Chateau Louise as a backdrop. This is a quintessential Banff experience.
day_by_day.evening: Drive or shuttle back to Banff. Freshen up at the hotel and enjoy a relaxed evening in town.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or at Laggan's Mountain Bakery in Lake Louise Village – famous for hearty baked goods and coffee, perfect pre-hike fuel (~CAD $10–$15).
meals.lunch: Stop at the Plain of Six Glaciers Teahouse on the trail (open July–September, cash only) for tea, soup, and homemade baked goods – a truly unique mid-hike dining experience (~CAD $15–$20).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Saltlik Steakhouse on Banff Avenue – quality Alberta beef steaks in a lively setting, mains ~CAD $35–$55. Treat yourself after a big hiking day.

day_by_day.notes: The Plain of Six Glaciers trail is 13.8 km with ~365m elevation gain – wear proper hiking boots and bring trekking poles if available. The Teahouse is cash only, so carry CAD $20–$25. Canoe rentals at Lake Louise Boathouse are first-come, first-served in the afternoon – arrive promptly after your hike.

day_by_day.morning: Johnston Canyon Waterfall Hike. Drive ~25 minutes west of Banff on the Bow Valley Parkway (Highway 1A). Walk the suspended catwalks carved into the canyon walls to reach the Lower Falls (2.4 km round trip, easy) and Upper Falls (5.4 km round trip, easy-moderate). The canyon is cool and shaded – ideal for a warm summer day. Arrive by 8:00 AM to secure parking and enjoy the canyon before crowds arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue along the Bow Valley Parkway back toward Banff, stopping at Castle Mountain Viewpoint for photos. Visit the Vermilion Lakes (just west of Banff townsite) for a peaceful lakeside walk with stunning Rundle Mountain reflections – a favourite spot for wildlife spotting (elk, beavers, birds).
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening in Banff. Browse the Whyte Museum of the Canadian Rockies (open until 5 PM, ~CAD $10 entry) for local history and art, then enjoy a leisurely dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel, then pack snacks for the canyon hike.
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch at Johnston Canyon picnic area or at Castle Mountain Viewpoint. Pick up supplies from Nesters Market the evening before.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Coyotes Southwestern Grill on Caribou Street – fresh, flavourful Southwestern-inspired dishes, vegetarian-friendly, mains ~CAD $22–$36. A local favourite.

day_by_day.notes: The Bow Valley Parkway (Highway 1A) is a scenic alternative to the Trans-Canada – drive slowly as wildlife sightings (deer, bears, wolves) are common. Johnston Canyon can get very busy by 10 AM on weekends; an early start is strongly recommended. The catwalks are family-friendly and accessible.

day_by_day.morning: Icefields Parkway Scenic Drive & Peyto Lake Viewpoint. Depart Banff by 8:00 AM and drive north on Highway 93 – one of the world's most spectacular roads. Stop at Bow Lake (stunning turquoise glacial lake, short lakeshore walk available), then continue to Bow Summit for the short but rewarding hike to Peyto Lake Viewpoint (~2.4 km round trip, moderate with some elevation). The wolf-head shaped turquoise lake surrounded by peaks is jaw-dropping.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue north on the Icefields Parkway to the Columbia Icefield Discovery Centre (~2 hours from Banff). Marvel at the Athabasca Glacier – walk to the glacier toe on the free self-guided path or opt for the Glacier Adventure (ice explorer bus, ~CAD $59/adult, book in advance). Begin the scenic drive back south to Banff, stopping at Sunwapta Falls and Mistaya Canyon if energy allows.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Banff by 6:00–7:00 PM. Relaxed dinner and early night to rest before the final full day.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departure.
meals.lunch: Pack a substantial trail lunch and snacks for the road – there are limited food options along the Parkway. Alternatively, grab a quick meal at the Columbia Icefield Discovery Centre cafeteria (~CAD $15–$20).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Bear Street Tavern – wood-fired pizza and craft beer in a cozy setting, mains ~CAD $18–$28. Perfect relaxed end to a long scenic day.

day_by_day.notes: Fill up your gas tank in Banff before departing – gas stations are scarce on the Icefields Parkway. The full Icefields Parkway round trip to the Columbia Icefield is ~430 km; allow a full day. Wildlife is frequently spotted along this route – keep eyes open for bears, bighorn sheep, and mountain goats. Book the Glacier Adventure in advance if interested.

day_by_day.morning: Sulphur Mountain Gondola & Summit Boardwalk Hike. Ride the Banff Gondola (~CAD $65/adult) to the summit of Sulphur Mountain at 2,281 metres for 360-degree panoramic views of six mountain ranges and the Banff townsite below. Walk the 1 km Summit Boardwalk to Sanson Peak and the historic weather observatory. Alternatively, hike up Sulphur Mountain Trail (9.4 km round trip, strenuous, ~655m elevation gain) and ride the gondola back down for a one-way ticket discount.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final afternoon in Banff – revisit your favourite spots. Consider a relaxing walk along the Bow River Trail, last-minute souvenir shopping on Banff Avenue, or a visit to the Cave and Basin National Historic Site (~CAD $8/adult) – the birthplace of Canada's national park system.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Banff before preparing for departure the next day. Pack bags and confirm transport to Calgary airport.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel breakfast or visit Evelyn's Coffee Bar on Banff Avenue for coffee and pastries – a beloved local spot (~CAD $10–$15).
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Sky Bistro at the top of the Sulphur Mountain Gondola – panoramic mountain views with a sit-down menu, mains ~CAD $25–$40. A special splurge with an unbeatable backdrop.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at The Maple Leaf Grille & Lounge on Banff Avenue – classic Canadian cuisine featuring Alberta beef, wild salmon, and local game in an elegant-casual setting, mains ~CAD $30–$50. A fitting final meal celebrating Canadian Rocky Mountain cuisine.

day_by_day.notes: If hiking up Sulphur Mountain, start by 8:00 AM to avoid afternoon heat and to have the summit to yourself before gondola crowds arrive. Check gondola operating hours and book tickets online in advance to skip the queue. Arrange your shuttle or rental car return to Calgary Airport (~1.5 hour drive) for the following morning if departing July 21.

day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Calgary International Airport at 14:00 on Flight AC. Collect luggage and meet your pre-arranged private luxury transfer to Banff Mountain Lodge (approx. 90-minute scenic drive through the foothills). Check in, settle into your room, and freshen up. Take a leisurely stroll along Banff Avenue to get oriented with the town, browse boutique shops, and soak in the mountain atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sunset walk along the Bow River Trail near the hotel for stunning early views of Cascade Mountain. Return to the lodge and prepare for a welcome dinner.

meals.lunch: Grab a light bite at the Calgary Airport's premium lounge or a quick stop en route at a café in Canmore.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Eden Restaurant at the Rimrock Resort Hotel — one of Banff's most celebrated fine-dining establishments offering contemporary Canadian cuisine with panoramic mountain views. Reserve the tasting menu with wine pairings.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Confirm check-in time with Banff Mountain Lodge ahead of arrival. Pick up your Parks Canada Discovery Pass at the park gate to cover entry fees for the week.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with a hearty breakfast at the lodge before heading out for the Sulphur Mountain Gondola & Summit Boardwalk Hike. Ride the Banff Gondola to 2,281 metres for breathtaking 360-degree panoramic views of six mountain ranges. Walk the 1-km summit boardwalk to Sanson's Peak and the historic Cosmic Ray Station. Arrive early (by 8:30 AM) to beat crowds and enjoy the crisp morning light on the peaks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to town and visit the Banff Upper Hot Springs for a luxurious soak in naturally heated mineral waters with mountain views — a perfect recovery after the gondola excursion. Spend the early afternoon exploring the Banff Park Museum and Whyte Museum of the Canadian Rockies for cultural context. Browse high-end boutiques along Banff Avenue.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the terrace of the Fairmont Banff Springs Hotel bar, soaking in the iconic castle-like architecture and valley views. Transition to dinner nearby.

meals.breakfast: Full hot breakfast at Banff Mountain Lodge or The Bison Restaurant & Terrace for locally sourced eggs, house-cured meats, and artisan pastries.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Sky Bistro at the top of the Sulphur Mountain Gondola — elevated Canadian cuisine with unmatched mountain panoramas.
meals.dinner: Dinner at The Maple Leaf Restaurant on Banff Avenue — celebrated for premium Canadian wild game, Alberta beef, and Pacific seafood in an elegant Rocky Mountain setting.

day_by_day.notes: Book Banff Gondola tickets online in advance to secure your preferred morning time slot. Hot Springs towel rental is available on-site. The Fairmont Banff Springs terrace can be busy; arrive by 7:00 PM for the best seating.

day_by_day.morning: Early departure (6:30 AM) to Moraine Lake to beat the mandatory Parks Canada reservation shuttle cutoff. Experience the Moraine Lake Valley of the Ten Peaks Trek — begin with the short but rewarding Rockpile Trail for the iconic elevated view over the impossibly blue glacial lake and the Valley of the Ten Peaks. Continue along the Lakeshore Trail for a peaceful 3.4 km round-trip walk at water level, with reflections of the peaks shimmering in the turquoise water.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the morning trek, enjoy a private guided canoe session on Moraine Lake, paddling the still glacial waters surrounded by towering peaks — a truly premium and unforgettable experience. Return to Banff by early afternoon for rest and refreshment at the lodge.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening in Banff town. Visit a local art gallery or enjoy a spa treatment at the hotel if available. Dinner at a top Banff restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Pre-packed gourmet picnic breakfast prepared by the lodge (request the night before) — enjoy it at the Moraine Lake lakeshore at sunrise.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Moraine Lake Lodge dining room (reservations essential) — refined lakeside dining with stunning views of the Ten Peaks.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Juniper Bistro at The Juniper Hotel — farm-to-table cuisine with a relaxed, sophisticated atmosphere and sweeping views of Mount Norquay and the Bow Valley.

day_by_day.notes: Moraine Lake road access requires a Parks Canada advance reservation or shuttle booking — secure this weeks in advance as it sells out quickly. Canoe rentals at Moraine Lake are available on a first-come basis; arriving early is strongly recommended. Wear layers as morning temperatures at the lake can be cool even in July.

day_by_day.morning: Drive the legendary Icefields Parkway (Highway 93) — widely regarded as one of the world's most scenic drives. Depart Banff by 8:00 AM heading north. Stop at the Bow Summit viewpoint (the highest drivable point on the Parkway at 2,069 m) for the short but spectacular hike to the Peyto Lake Viewpoint. The wolf-head shaped turquoise lake framed by ancient glaciers and dense boreal forest is an absolute highlight of the Canadian Rockies.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue north along the Parkway to the Columbia Icefield area. Visit the Glacier Skywalk — a glass-floored observation platform cantilevered over the Sunwapta Valley — and take a guided Ice Explorer tour onto the Athabasca Glacier for a once-in-a-lifetime walk on a 10,000-year-old glacier. Begin the return journey south along the Parkway, stopping at Sunwapta Falls and Athabasca Falls for short scenic walks.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Banff by early evening (approximately 6:30–7:00 PM). Unwind at the lodge before a celebratory mid-trip dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the lodge before departure — request an early seating or grab a gourmet to-go option from the hotel.
meals.lunch: Packed premium picnic lunch prepared by the lodge, enjoyed at a scenic pullout along the Icefields Parkway — consider Waterfowl Lakes or Mistaya Canyon as a stunning backdrop.
meals.dinner: Dinner at The Grapes Wine Bar at the Fairmont Banff Springs — an extensive wine list paired with refined small plates and charcuterie in an intimate, elegant setting.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Glacier Skywalk and Ice Explorer Athabasca Glacier tour online well in advance — these are extremely popular in July. Bring warm layers regardless of summer temperatures; the glacier and high-altitude stops are significantly cooler. Fill up the car with gas in Banff before departing as fuel stations along the Parkway are limited. Allow a full day — approximately 10–11 hours round trip with stops.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Johnston Canyon for the Johnston Canyon Waterfall Hike — one of the most dramatic canyon walks in the Rockies. Walk along suspended catwalks bolted into the canyon walls above the rushing creek to reach the Lower Falls (1.1 km) and then continue to the spectacular Upper Falls (2.7 km). Depart by 7:30 AM to enjoy the canyon in soft morning light and before tour groups arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: After Johnston Canyon, drive to Lake Louise (approximately 45 minutes). Embark on the Lake Louise Hike & Canoe experience — hike the iconic Plain of Six Glaciers Trail along the lakeshore and up into the alpine meadows above Lake Louise, with jaw-dropping views of Victoria Glacier and the surrounding peaks. The full trail is approximately 13.8 km return with 365 m elevation gain. For a shorter option, hike to the Plain of Six Glaciers Teahouse (8.6 km return) and reward yourself with tea and homemade baked goods.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Banff for a relaxed and indulgent final full-day evening. Optional: book an in-room spa treatment or private hot tub session at the lodge.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the lodge before early departure.
meals.lunch: Tea and homemade scones, soups, and baked goods at the legendary Plain of Six Glaciers Teahouse — a historic alpine hut serving hikers since 1927 (cash only; bring small bills).
meals.dinner: Farewell-style premium dinner at 1888 Chop House inside the Fairmont Banff Springs — renowned for dry-aged Alberta beef, fresh seafood towers, and an award-winning wine cellar in a grand historic dining room.

day_by_day.notes: Johnston Canyon can be slippery on the catwalks — wear grippy hiking footwear. The Plain of Six Glaciers Teahouse is only accessible on foot and operates seasonally (typically mid-June to early October, weather permitting). Confirm it is open before departure. The Lake Louise parking lot fills extremely early in summer — arrive before 8:00 AM or use the Parks Canada shuttle from the Lake Louise Ski Resort overflow lot.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Banff. Wake up early for a peaceful sunrise walk along the Bow River or a gentle stroll up to Tunnel Mountain viewpoint (2.3 km loop from town) for sweeping last views over the Bow Valley, Banff townsite, and surrounding peaks. Return to the lodge for a leisurely checkout breakfast and pack up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time, enjoy a final browse of Banff Avenue for premium souvenirs — locally made artisan goods, Canadian maple products, and Rocky Mountain-themed gifts. Visit the Banff Visitor Centre for any last-minute national park mementos. Private luxury transfer departs Banff for Calgary International Airport (allow at least 2.5 hours before flight for the drive and check-in).
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Calgary International Airport. If the flight is late evening, consider a stop in Canmore for a final meal at the acclaimed Tavern 1883 or Murrieta's Bar & Grill before heading to the airport.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely final breakfast at Coyotes Southwestern Grill in Banff — beloved local institution with vibrant flavours, fresh ingredients, and a relaxed atmosphere perfect for a final morning.
meals.lunch: Light lunch or charcuterie board at Bear Street Tavern on Bear Street — artisan pizza, craft beer, and casual mountain-chic atmosphere for a relaxed send-off.
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or an early dinner in Canmore at The Trough Dining Co. — sophisticated farm-to-table cuisine highlighting Alberta and Canadian ingredients, ideal for a memorable final meal.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm private transfer booking the evening before. Check out time at Banff Mountain Lodge is typically 11:00 AM — request a late checkout if the flight schedule allows. Ensure all Parks Canada passes and rental equipment are returned. Calgary Airport security and customs can be lengthy in peak summer season — allow ample time.
